spectrum_continuous_help: A hot, dense source makes a smooth spectrum. This teaching view has no sharp lines to track.
spectrum_emission_help: Excited, thin hydrogen gas produces bright lines. Their positions identify the gas and reveal its radial motion.
spectrum_absorption_help: Hydrogen gas in front of a hotter background absorbs light at characteristic wavelengths, leaving dark lines.
spectrum_at_rest: At rest along the line of sight
spectrum_no_lines: Choose emission or absorption to activate the line close-up and Doppler controls.
spectrum_overview_help: Four hydrogen lines are shown. The gold pointer identifies the selected line; small Doppler shifts are easier to see in the close-up.
spectrum_zoom_help: The close-up spans 2.5 nm around the rest wavelength. Its horizontal scale magnifies displacement by 148×. The line profiles illustrate peaks or dips; their widths and strengths are teaching choices.
spectrum_intro: Compare continuous light with bright emission lines and dark absorption lines. Choose a hydrogen line, then move the radial velocity to see its wavelength shift.
spectrum_velocity_help: Negative velocity means approaching; positive means moving away. Arrow keys step by 10 km/s. Home and End reach −300 and +300 km/s.
spectrum_model_scope: Reference wavelengths are in vacuum, matching the cosmic redshift lab. Velocities and line profiles are teaching examples. The calculation uses the relativistic Doppler relation for motion directly along the line of sight. Expanding space and gravitational shifts are separate effects.
